name: Autosomal Dominant Hereditary Chronic Pancreatitis

criteria.description: Presence of chronic pancreatitis in at least two first-degree relatives in two or more generations consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Recurrent episodes of pancreatitis or chronic pancreatitis symptoms including abdominal pain and pancreatic insufficiency
Identification of pathogenic variants in PRSS1 gene or other associated genes (e.g., SPINK1, CTRC)
Imaging evidence of pancreatic ductal irregularities, calcifications, or atrophy consistent with chronic pancreatitis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical features with a positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance; genetic testing supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but absence of mutation does not exclude diagnosis due to genetic heterogeneity.

laboratory: Elevated serum amylase and lipase during acute attacks
Fecal elastase deficiency indicating exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
Hyperglycemia in cases with endocrine insufficiency
imaging: Pancreatic ductal irregularities and dilatation on MRCP or ERCP
Pancreatic calcifications on abdominal CT or X-ray
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Histopathology showing fibrosis and acinar cell loss in pancreatic tissue

distinguishingFeatures: Younger age of onset with distinct clinical features

redFlags: Rapid progression to pancreatic exocrine and endocrine insufficiency
Severe, unremitting abdominal pain refractory to standard therapy
references: Whitcomb DC. Hereditary pancreatitis: new insights into acute and chronic pancreatitis. Gut. 1999;45(3):317-322.
Rosendahl J, et al. Hereditary pancreatitis: clinical features and genetic mutations. Pancreatology. 2013;13(1):1-7.
